children: Modella Capital
, the private‑equity owner of TG Jones and Flying Tiger Copenhagen, has been weighing a bid for British fashion brand Joseph, according to
The Sunday Times

. The 60‑year‑old label, founded by Joseph Ettedgui and known for its 1990s heyday, appointed PwC to run a sale process earlier this year, with one round of bids already completed and the next due in mid‑November. Joseph has been owned by Japan's
Onward Kashiyama
since 2005, but has struggled in recent years, posting turnover of £45m last year, down from £56m. Modella was said to be among several suitors circling the business.
Kemi Badenoch has accused chancellor John Healey of leaving a £49bn gap in the public finances that she says will force Labour into substantial tax rises,
The Telegraph

reported. Writing in the paper, the Conservative leader claimed Labour would need to raise taxes by £1,700 per household by 2030/31 to fund unfunded commitments, including an £11bn defence shortfall, up to £17bn for a National Care Service, £4bn for council‑house building and additional departmental spending to avoid real‑terms cuts. Badenoch said "the worst is yet to come", arguing Labour would have to raise taxes further to meet its promises.
A US federal judge has dismissed Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against
the Wall Street Journal
over its reporting on an alleged birthday message to Jeffrey Epstein,
The Telegraph

reported. Judge Darrin Gayles ruled that Trump had again failed to demonstrate actual malice, throwing out the case with prejudice after previously allowing him to amend the claim. Gayles said the allegations were "conclusory, vague, sometimes inconsistent" and lacked merit. Trump's legal team said he would appeal, insisting he would continue to challenge what he calls "Fake News and smears".
Binance
has replaced around 90% of the $6.3bn stolen in a record hack attributed by the FBI to North Korea‑backed group TraderTraitor,
The Guardian

reported. The remaining 10% consists of less liquid tokens that will take longer to buy, though co‑CEO Richard Teng said Binance was committed to covering the balance so users would not bear losses. Withdrawals, suspended after the attack, have begun reopening in phases. The FBI confirmed TraderTraitor's involvement, linking it to the Lazarus Group, known for the 2014
Sony Pictures
hack.

Hundreds of high‑street "slot farms" could continue receiving business rates discounts intended for leisure venues unless the government closes a loophole allowing them to operate under bingo licences,
The Guardian

reported. Chancellor John Healey raised duty on slot‑machine takings and said adult gaming centres and vape shops would lose access to hospitality sector rate relief. However, analysis suggests many venues owned by
Merkur
and
Admiral
may still qualify because they hold bingo licences despite offering mainly slot machines. Andy Burnham has publicly backed the crackdown as part of his high street agenda.
Reporting by Iain Gilbert at Sharecast.com
